key_insight: Path to Prevention (P2P) is a phase 2A platform trial designed to test interventions in early-stage neuronal α-synuclein disease before clinically defined Parkinson’s disease or a related disorder.
clinical_relevance: The trial targets adults aged 60 or older with abnormal α-synuclein, dopaminergic dysfunction, and prodromal signs or symptoms but no functional impairment.
method: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled platform embedded within the observational PPMI cohort.
Approximately 35 North American and European sites; 125 active-treatment participants and at least 125 shared placebo participants per regimen.
Two primary endpoints track putamen dopamine-transporter binding and MDS-UPDRS Part III motor scores.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a study design, not efficacy results, with treatment lasting up to 144 weeks and Bayesian modeling incorporating data from non-enrolled PPMI participants.
watch_item: Whether treatment at this biological stage delays clinically meaningful disease progression remains unproven; this paper is not about AI or cancer drug discovery.
paper_title: Path to Prevention Platform Trial in Early-Stage Neuronal Alpha-Synuclein Disease: Study Design
